title: Pneumothorax: Lung Edge, Deep Sulcus and Tension Clues
subject: Radiological Signs
preview: Pneumothorax may show a visceral pleural line with absent peripheral lung markings.
quickRevision: Pneumothorax may show a visceral pleural line with absent peripheral lung markings.
Tension pneumothorax is primarily a clinical emergency when severe respiratory or hemodynamic compromise is present.
Ultrasound can support bedside diagnosis where appropriate, but interpretation depends on operator skill and context.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Pneumothorax may show a visceral pleural line with absent peripheral lung markings.
In supine imaging, a deep sulcus sign can be an indirect clue to pneumothorax.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Tension pneumothorax is primarily a clinical emergency when severe respiratory or hemodynamic compromise is present.
Ultrasound can support bedside diagnosis where appropriate, but interpretation depends on operator skill and context.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not delay urgent decompression for radiography in a critically unstable patient with convincing tension physiology.
